reason: Reads each argument of a console message as a JSHandle (`args()[n].jsonValue()`); a `ConsoleMessage` carries the formatted text, level, and location, not the arguments

Inspects a console message with Node's `util.inspect`, which prints the text because Playwright's message defines an inspect hook; Strider's message is a Schema value with no hook, and its text is the `text` field

Checks a message's `type()` as timeEnd, trace, dir, timeLog, and so on; Strider's level has five values (debug, log, info, warning, error), so those types have no name. The matrix row says the type is present, which covers only the five levels

Checks a message's wall-clock timestamp against the test's clock (CM-014, CM-016), or that the timestamps of successive messages don't decrease (CM-015); a `ConsoleMessage`'s `at` is when Strider received the message, a monotonic instant, not the browser's time of the call, and there is no timestamp
Clears a page's console messages so that later reads start from the clear; Strider's history is read but not cleared
Reads a page's console messages either since its last navigation or all of them; `ConsoleMessage.history` has no navigation filter
Reads a page's uncaught exceptions either since its last navigation or all of them; `UncaughtException.history` has no navigation filter
